titleEn: The 12th-century Chinese poet who was among the first to explore the inner lives of cats
titleZh: 探索猫咪内心世界的先驱：一位十二世纪中国诗人
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: If you’re reading this, then your media feed, like mine, is probably full of cats.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你正在阅读这篇文章，那么你的媒体提要，就像我的一样，可能充满了猫。

paragraphs.en: That’s hardly surprising. The internet has always belonged to cats, which suits me just fine: I love cats and live with four of them.
paragraphs.zh: 这并不奇怪，互联网一直属于猫，这正适合我：我喜欢猫，和四只猫一起生活。

paragraphs.en: But in one of the classes I’ve taught, “Cats: Why We Love Them,” I explain how our affection for the house cat, Felis silvestris catus, is a relatively recent phenomenon in the scope of human history. In many parts of the world, cats were viewed with suspicion and subjected to terrible mistreatment.
paragraphs.zh: 但在我教过的一门课“猫：我们为什么爱它们”中，我解释了我们对家猫Felis silvestris卡图斯的喜爱是人类历史上一个相对较新的现象。在世界上的许多地方，猫被怀疑并受到可怕的虐待。

paragraphs.en: Of course, the ancient Egyptians loved cats – this can be seen in sculptures, paintings and even mummified cat remains. Meanwhile, premodern poets, writers and artists were among the first to wonder about the inner lives of cats – and to explore how caring for them might expand our capacity for empathy.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，古埃及人喜欢猫--这一点在雕塑、绘画，甚至是猫的木乃伊中都可以看到。与此同时，前现代的诗人、作家和艺术家也是最早对猫的内心生活产生好奇心的人之一--他们还探索了如何通过照顾猫来增强我们的同理心。

paragraphs.en: One of the earliest literary accounts of a cat is the ninth-century poem “Pangur Bán,” written by an unnamed Irish monk. In the poem, he describes the parallels between his devotion to hunting for meaning in the texts he is studying and the cat’s devotion to hunting mice.
paragraphs.zh: 关于猫的最早的文学作品之一是9世纪的一首诗《潘古尔·班》（Pangur Bán），作者是一位不知名的爱尔兰修道士。在这首诗中，他描述了自己在研究文本中寻找意义的献身精神与猫猎杀老鼠的献身精神之间的相似之处。

paragraphs.en: What’s interesting about the poem is how the anonymous poet sees the cat as possessing qualities that resemble human qualities – and, in doing so, implicitly suggests that cats have dignity much like human dignity.
paragraphs.zh: 这首诗的有趣之处在于，这位匿名诗人是如何将猫视为拥有类似人类品质的品质的--而且，这样做隐含地暗示了猫有着与人类尊严很相似的尊严。

paragraphs.en: The monk does not set himself above the cat in some great hierarchy of life, but instead places himself alongside the cat as peers in their dedicated practices.
paragraphs.zh: 僧侣并没有把自己置于猫之上，而是把自己放在猫的旁边，在他们专注的实践中作为同伴。

paragraphs.en: Lu You’s cat
paragraphs.zh: 陆游的猫

paragraphs.en: In the 12th century, the Chinese poet Lu You composed over 9,000 poems. A handful were about his cats, and of these, three are entitled “Zeng mao,” or “Presented to My Cat.” It’s not clear if the poems are all about the same cat, as Lu had more than one cat over his lifetime.
paragraphs.zh: 世纪，中国诗人陆游创作了9,000多首诗。其中有几首是关于他的猫的，其中有三首题为“赠猫”。目前还不清楚这些诗是否都是关于同一只猫的，因为陆游一生中养过不止一只猫。

paragraphs.en: In Chinese literature, poems that include the term “zeng” – “to present” – are often sent to acquaintances as a form of literary exchange. Prior to Lu, there’s no literary evidence that anyone had addressed a poem to a cat.
paragraphs.zh: 在中国文学中，含有“赠”字的诗通常被作为一种文学交流的形式送给熟人。在陆游之前，没有文学证据表明有人给猫写过诗。

paragraphs.en: In the first poem, Lu begins by explaining that he acquired a cat to protect his library from vermin. Looking around his home, he feels embarrassed by his lack of success in life:
paragraphs.zh: 在第一首诗中，陆兆禧首先解释说，他养了一只猫，以保护他的图书馆免受害虫的侵害。环顾他的家，他为自己在生活中的不成功感到尴尬：

paragraphs.en: I’m ashamed that I’m poor and my achievements few,
paragraphs.zh: 愧贫绩寡，

paragraphs.en: When you’re cold there’s no rug, when I feed you there’s no fish.
paragraphs.zh: 你冷的时候没有毯子，我喂你的时候没有鱼。

paragraphs.en: In the second of these poems, a longer eight-line poem, the poet accuses his cat of poor feline behavior familiar even today:
paragraphs.zh: 在第二首较长的八行诗中，诗人指责他的猫的可怜的猫行为，即使在今天也很常见：

paragraphs.en: You frequently get drunk from catnip,
paragraphs.zh: 你经常喝猫薄荷喝醉，

paragraphs.en: You commandeer the blanket every night.
paragraphs.zh: 你每天晚上都霸占毯子。

paragraphs.en: But he follows with praise for the cat’s achievements:
paragraphs.zh: 但他随后对猫的成就表示赞赏：

paragraphs.en: Deeds of the mousehole – just now recounted,
paragraphs.zh: 鼠洞的事迹-刚才叙述，

paragraphs.en: Rewards of fish morsels – how could these be omitted?
paragraphs.zh: 奖励的鱼块-这些怎么能被省略？

paragraphs.en: He ends by naming the cat:
paragraphs.zh: 最后，他给猫起了个名字：

paragraphs.en: Still, I should give you a name,
paragraphs.zh: 不过，我还是应该给你个名字，

paragraphs.en: I’ll call you “Little Tiger.”
paragraphs.zh: 我就叫你小老虎

paragraphs.en: Lu chooses a name that probably was given to countless cats in premodern China. But by ending the poem with the act of naming, he is emphasizing how this cat is an individual to him, known to him by this name and none other.
paragraphs.zh: 陆川选择了一个可能是前现代中国无数猫的名字。但通过以命名的行为结束这首诗，他强调了这只猫对他来说是一个个体，他只知道这个名字。

paragraphs.en: Poet and cat, late in life
paragraphs.zh: 诗人和猫，晚年

paragraphs.en: The relationship that Lu depicts between cat and human will be familiar to anyone who has fought with their cat over who gets the blanket or wondered what their cat might be thinking.
paragraphs.zh: 卢描绘的猫和人之间的关系对任何人来说都是熟悉的，他们和他们的猫为了谁得到毯子而争吵，或者想知道他们的猫可能在想什么。

paragraphs.en: The third poem, translated here in full, finds the cat late in its life, with its days chasing mice long behind it. Its poignancy is amplified by the fact that Lu composed it in the last year of his own life:
paragraphs.zh: 第三首诗，全文翻译如下：这只猫已经到了晚年，追逐老鼠的日子已经过去很久了。这首诗的辛酸之处在于，它是陆兆禧在自己生命的最后一年写的：

paragraphs.en: As for catching mice you lack merit, but I never complain,
paragraphs.zh: 至于捉老鼠，你没有功劳，但我从不抱怨，

paragraphs.en: A ladle of fish and rice will come at the usual time.
paragraphs.zh: 一勺鱼和米饭会在平常的时间送来。

paragraphs.en: Throughout the day I see you sleeping peacefully,
paragraphs.zh: 一整天我都看到你安然入睡，

paragraphs.en: So why am I always coming and going?
paragraphs.zh: 为什么我总是来来去去？

paragraphs.en: Lu sees himself through the bemused eyes of the cat, who’s perhaps wondering why this foolish old man is rushing to and fro, fulfilling goals and seeking praise, when he might just be satisfied with what he already has.
paragraphs.zh: 卢通过猫困惑的眼睛看到了自己，猫也许在想，为什么这个愚蠢的老人在来回奔波，完成目标，寻求赞美，而他可能只是满足于他已经拥有的东西。

paragraphs.en: And despite his cat’s indolence, Lu continues to cherish his feline, making sure to regularly serve its dinner. This is significant, given that other premodern Chinese writers viewed cats primarily as vermin-catchers that should be replaced once they outlive their usefulness.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管他的猫很懒，但陆继续珍惜他的猫，确保定期为它提供晚餐。这很重要，因为其他前现代中国作家认为猫主要是害虫捕手，一旦它们失去了使用价值，就应该被取代。

paragraphs.en: Personhood and care
paragraphs.zh: 人格与关怀

paragraphs.en: Imagining oneself as a pampered cat will be familiar to those of us who live with cats – a thought-experiment that is tinged with more than a little envy for the capacity to live in the moment, without anxiety over the future.
paragraphs.zh: 想象自己是一只娇生惯养的猫，这对我们这些和猫生活在一起的人来说是很熟悉的--这是一个思想实验，对生活在当下的能力充满了嫉妒，而不对未来感到焦虑。

paragraphs.en: Lu’s care for his cat affords him the possibility of imagining a nonhuman animal mind. The poet learns something from his cat in the end, as he imagines the world through the cat’s eyes and, in doing so, perhaps finds a measure of solace.
paragraphs.zh: 对猫的照顾，让他有可能想像出一种非人类的动物心灵。诗人最后从猫身上学到了一些东西，因为他通过猫的眼睛想象世界，并在这样做的过程中找到了某种安慰。

paragraphs.en: Lu does not speak in the language of what philosophers call moral personhood. He is not reflecting on the broader ethical question of which creatures deserve to be treated with care and respect.
paragraphs.zh: 吕不韦并没有用哲学家所谓的道德人格的语言来说话，他没有思考更广泛的伦理问题，即哪些生物应该得到照顾和尊重。

paragraphs.en: But I argue that his actions nonetheless demonstrate how he treats his cat as somewhat of an equal. This can be seen, not least of all, by how he addresses poems to his cat, an act of social exchange that was heretofore reserved for literary interactions with other human beings.
paragraphs.zh: 但我认为，他的行为仍然表明，他是如何对待他的猫的，这可以看出，尤其是，他如何向他的猫写诗，这是一种社会交换行为，在此之前，这种行为只适用于与其他人的文学互动。

paragraphs.en: Personhood – the recognition of an individual as deserving of dignity – is often assumed the sole province of human beings. But philosopher María Puig de la Bellacasa has promoted a worldview that she calls “more than human thinking,” which urges people to broaden their scope of moral concern, and in this way, enlarge human capacities for care and love. The philosopher Lori Gruen similarly conceives of an “entangled empathy,” calling attention to the complex relational intimacies that bind human and nonhuman animals together. They insist that human lives are better when the sphere of care and concern is extended to those creatures with whom human lives are entangled.
paragraphs.zh: 人格--承认一个人值得拥有尊严--通常被认为是人类的唯一领域。但哲学家玛丽亚·普伊格·德拉贝拉卡萨（María Puig de la Bellacasa）提倡一种她称之为“超越人类思维”的世界观，这种世界观敦促人们拓宽道德关注的范围，并通过这种方式扩大人类关心和爱的能力。哲学家洛里·格鲁恩（Lori Gruen）同样设想了一种“纠结的同理心，“呼吁人们关注将人类和非人类动物联系在一起的复杂的关系亲密性。他们坚持认为，当关怀和关心的范围扩大到与人类生活纠缠在一起的那些生物时，人类的生活会更好。

paragraphs.en: Born in the 12th century, Lu You could not be expected to argue for animal rights. But he clearly understands that his cat has claims to happiness, pleasure, comfort and companionship, and that while the cat might see the world differently than he does, that doesn’t diminish its claim to empathy and love.
paragraphs.zh: 出生于12世纪世纪的陆游不会为动物权利辩护。但他清楚地知道，他的猫有权利享受幸福、快乐、舒适和陪伴，尽管猫可能看世界的方式与他不同，但这并不影响它对同情和爱的要求。
